proposals.before: In his thirteenth year he died on the road at Guizhou, aged forty; he was buried at Ruiling, posthumously made Prince of Lu with the posthumous name Xiangmu.
proposals.after: In the thirteenth year he died on the road at Guizhou, aged forty; he was buried at Ruiling, posthumously made Prince of Lu with the posthumous name Xiangmu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 十三年 is a regnal year (Tianhui 13), not 'his thirteenth year', which wrongly suggests age.

proposals.before: Bachao was sent to strike the Song emperor at Yangzhou; the Song court got wind of it and crossed the river the night before he arrived.
proposals.after: Bachao and others were sent to strike the Song ruler at Yangzhou; the Song ruler heard of it and, the night before Bachao reached Yangzhou, had already crossed the Yangtze.
proposals.reason: Omits 等 ('and others') and replaces 宋主 with 'Song court' in the second clause, losing the ruler as subject.

proposals.before: Ritual Department Director Li Bangzhi and Vice Director Li Shan lost one grade; Vice Minister of Rites Wu Zhicai, Director Zhang Ziyu, and Academician Zhang Ju lost two.
proposals.after: Ritual Department Director Li Bangzhi and Vice Director Li Shan lost one grade; Chamberlain for Ceremonials Wu Zhicai, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Director Zhang Ziyu, and Erudite Zhang Ju lost two.
proposals.reason: 太常少卿/太常丞 are Court of Imperial Sacrifices offices, not the Ritual Department (禮部); conflating them with 'Rites' is misleading.

proposals.before: In the fifth month, on renyin, he was made crown prince, and Shizong said to him, "Ritual honors the legitimate heir—that is why you are named.
proposals.after: In the fifth month, on renyin, he was made crown prince, and Shizong said to him, "Ritual honors the legitimate heir—that is why you are set up.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 世守 (likely 世宗); English already has Shizong. Closing quote incomplete vs Chinese clause boundary is OK; 'named' understates 立卿 'installed you'.

proposals.before: In the eighth month of the tenth year, at the classics lecture in Chenghua Hall, Crown Prince Grand Guardian Prince Shou Shuang said, "Your Highness is still weak in our tongue—why not dismiss the Han officials around you and use only Jurchens?"
proposals.after: In the eighth month of the tenth year, while the crown prince was at the classics lecture in Chenghua Hall, Crown Prince Grand Guardian Prince Shou Shuang said, "Your Highness is still weak in our tongue—why not dismiss the Han officials around you and use only Jurchens?"
proposals.reason: Chinese 帝在承華殿經筵 states the heir was at the lecture; the idiomatic omits that subject and can be read as if only Shuang is located there.

proposals.before: Shizong said: "When ordinary men adopt a son, they all hope that in old age he will prove useful.
proposals.after: Shizong said: "When ordinary men raise a son, they all hope that in old age he will prove useful.
proposals.reason: Chinese 養子 here means rearing a son, not legal adoption; the idiomatic correctly has 'raise a son'.

proposals.before: Third month: Shizong went to the Upper Capital as above; the Heir guarded the realm and remained at Zhongdu.
proposals.after: Third month: Shizong went to the Upper Capital; the Heir guarded the realm and remained at Zhongdu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 如上京 means went to the Upper Capital (如 = go to); as above mistranslates 如.

proposals.before: Since taking the regency he had been deeply modest: palace officers did not bow in court; at memorials he did not stand by; new-moon and full-moon audiences were suspended.
proposals.after: Since taking the regency he had been deeply modest: palace officers did not bow in court; when presenting affairs they did not stand in attendance; new-moon and full-moon audiences were suspended.
proposals.reason: 啟事時不侍立 takes palace officers as subject; they did not stand attendant, not the heir.

proposals.before: Shizong put Prince of Bin Yongcheng in charge at the Central Capital, sent Zai Xing, chief steward of the Prince of Teng’s house, and Palace Service Commissioner Alila to guard the Prince of Jinyuan, sent Left Imperial Wardrobe Commissioner Tangkuo Ding with offerings, and ordered Consort Tudan and the imperial grandsons to mourn by Han custom.
proposals.after: Shizong put Prince of Bin Yongcheng in charge at the Central Capital, sent Zai Xing, chief steward of the Prince of Teng’s house, and Palace Service Commissioner Alila to guard the Prince of Jinyuan, sent Left Xuanhui Commissioner Tangkuo Ding with offerings, and ordered Consort Tudan and the imperial grandsons to mourn by Han custom.
proposals.reason: 左宣徽使 is Left Xuanhui Commissioner, not an Imperial Wardrobe office.

proposals.before: When property was lost he made the loser pay compensation but imposed no further penalty.
proposals.after: When property was lost he made those responsible for the loss pay compensation but imposed no further penalty.
proposals.reason: 亡失物者 means the party responsible for losing the goods; 'the loser' is ambiguous and can reverse the sense.

proposals.before: When Empress Mingde was buried at Kunhou and consorts were enshrined with her, the procession left Panning Palace; Prince of Zhao Wei Zhong sent his mother’s bier ahead and yellow canopies forward; the emperor called the bearers and got no answer; Junior Palace Steward Zhang Jinyan would have reported it, but the emperor stopped him.
proposals.after: When Empress Mingde was buried at Kunhou and consorts were enshrined with her, the procession left Panning Palace; Wei Zhong, Prince of Zhao, sent his mother’s bier ahead and yellow canopies forward; the emperor called the bearers and got no answer; Junior Palace Steward Zhang Jinyan would have reported it, but the emperor stopped him.
proposals.reason: 趙王惟中 is title plus personal name Wei Zhong; 'Prince of Zhao Wei Zhong' wrongly reads Zhao as part of the personal name.

proposals.before: Comment: Prince of Liao Gao took the Zhong Capital; Zonghan and Zongwang followed, while Jingxuan separately led the hezha meng'an.
proposals.after: Comment: Gao, Prince of Liao, took the Zhong Capital; Zonghan and Zongwang followed, while Jingxuan separately led the hezha meng'an.
proposals.reason: 遼王杲 is title plus personal name Gao; 'Prince of Liao Gao' wrongly reads Liao as part of the personal name.

proposals.before: In the thirteenth year, on campaign he died at Guizhou, aged forty; he was buried beside Ruiling, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Lu, posthumous name Xiangmu.
proposals.after: In Tianhui 13, he died while traveling through Guizhou, aged forty; he was buried beside Ruiling and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Lu, with the posthumous name Xiangmu.
proposals.reason: The literal field should identify the regnal year and render 行次 as dying while traveling, not necessarily on campaign.

proposals.before: Bachao and others were sent to strike the Song ruler at Yangzhou, but the Song ruler heard of it and, the night before Bachao reached Yangzhou, had already crossed the Yangtze.
proposals.after: Bagaosu and others were sent to make a surprise attack on the Song ruler at Yangzhou, but the Song ruler learned of it and had already crossed the Yangtze the night before Bagaosu reached Yangzhou.
proposals.reason: The literal field has the correct subjects but mistranscribes the personal name 拔高速 as Bachao rather than Bagaosu.

proposals.before: Thereupon Ritual Department Director Li Bangzhi and Vice Director Li Shan were reduced one grade, and Vice Minister of Rites Wu Zhicai, Director Zhang Ziyu, and Academician Zhang Ju were reduced two grades.
proposals.after: Thereupon Director in the Ministry of Rites Li Bangzhi and Vice Director Li Shan were demoted one grade; Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wu Zhicai, Assistant Director Zhang Ziyu, and Erudite Zhang Ju were demoted two grades.
proposals.reason: The literal field also conflates 太常 offices with the Ministry of Rites and obscures the hierarchy between 少卿 and 丞.

proposals.before: Fifth month, renyin: he was installed as crown prince, and Shizong told him: "By ritual the legitimate son is honored—that is why you are set up.
proposals.after: Fifth month, renyin: he was installed as crown prince, and Shizong told him: "Ritual honors the legitimate heir; that is why I have installed you.
proposals.reason: The literal field's 'set up' is not idiomatic English for 立卿 and obscures Shizong as the agent.

proposals.before: Since keeping the realm the emperor had been deeply modest: palace officers did not bow in court; at memorials he did not stand in attendance; new-moon and full-moon rites were waived.
proposals.after: Since taking responsibility for the realm, the heir was deeply modest: palace officers did not make court obeisance to him, and he did not require them to stand in attendance when presenting matters; the new-moon and full-moon rites were waived.
proposals.reason: The literal field assigns 不侍立 to the heir himself; the passage describes the ceremonial privileges he waived for his palace officers.

proposals.before: Shizong made Prince of Bin Yongcheng Central Capital regent to oversee the mourning, sent Chief Steward Zai Xing of the Prince of Teng’s establishment and Palace Service Commissioner Alila to protect Prince of Jinyuan, sent Left Commissioner of the Imperial Wardrobe Tangkuo Ding to offer sacrifice, and ordered Consort Tudan and all imperial grandsons to wear mourning by Han rites.
proposals.after: Shizong appointed Yongcheng, Prince of Bin, as Stay-behind of the Central Capital, and he came to supervise the mourning. Shizong sent Zaixing, chief steward of the Prince of Teng's household, and Palace Service Commissioner Alila to protect the Prince of Jinyuan; sent Tangkuo Ding, Left Xuanhui Commissioner, to present sacrifices; and ordered Consort Tudan and all the imperial grandsons to observe mourning according to Han custom.
proposals.reason: The literal field mistranslates 左宣徽使, splits Zaixing's given name, and obscures Yongcheng's title and role in the mourning.

proposals.before: When things were lost he made the loser compensate but added no crime.
proposals.after: Those who lost property were required to compensate for it but incurred no further penalty.
proposals.reason: The literal field is unidiomatic and 'the loser' can be mistaken for the owner rather than the person responsible for the loss.

proposals.before: When Empress Mingde was buried at Kunhou Tomb and all consorts were enshrined with her, the procession left Panning Palace; Prince of Zhao Wei Zhong had his mother’s bier carriage set out first and ordered men with yellow canopies to go ahead; the emperor called to the canopy-bearers and got no answer; Junior Palace Steward Zhang Jinyan wished to memorialize it, but the emperor stopped him.
proposals.after: When Empress Mingde was buried in Kunhou Mausoleum, all the consorts were buried alongside her. As the procession departed Panning Palace, Weizhong, Prince of Zhao, had his mother's funeral carriage set out first and ordered the yellow-canopy bearers to walk ahead. The emperor called to the canopy bearers, but they did not answer. Junior Palace Steward Zhang Jinyan wished to memorialize the matter, but the emperor stopped him.
proposals.reason: The literal field misorders Weizhong's title and name, splits his given name, and renders funerary 祔 as enshrinement rather than accompanying burial.

proposals.before: Comment: Prince of Liao Gao took the Zhong Capital; Zonghan and Zongwang both followed, while Jingxuan separately commanded the hezha meng'an.
proposals.after: Appraisal: Gao, Prince of Liao, captured the Central Capital; Zonghan and Zongwang both followed him, while Jingxuan separately commanded the hezha meng'an.
proposals.reason: The literal field also misorders Gao's title and name; 贊曰 introduces the historian's appraisal.

proposals.before: In the thirteenth year, tenth month, by edict he hunted with the Prince of Zhao, Wei Zhong, and the Prince of Cao, Wei Gong, in Bao and Ding prefectures.
proposals.after: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year, by edict he hunted with Weizhong, Prince of Zhao, and Weigong, Prince of Cao, in Bao and Ding prefectures.
proposals.reason: 惟中 and 惟功 are two-syllable given names, Weizhong and Weigong; the existing punctuation makes the titles look like separate people.

proposals.before: Thirteenth year, tenth month: by imperial order he hunted with Prince of Zhao Wei Zhong and Prince of Cao Wei Gong in Bao and Ding prefectures.
proposals.after: Thirteenth year, tenth month: by imperial order he hunted with Weizhong, Prince of Zhao, and Weigong, Prince of Cao, in Bao and Ding prefectures.
proposals.reason: The literal field likewise splits the two given names and misorders each title-name phrase.

decisions.after: In Tianhui 13, he died while traveling through Guizhou at the age of forty. He was buried beside Ruiling and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Lu, with the posthumous name Xiangmu.
decisions.reason: 十三年 is Tianhui 13 (1135), not the subject's thirteenth year; 陪葬 places his burial beside Ruiling.
